surfaces.part: bone fragments scattered flat on the floor

answer.evidence: The sprite is a sparse set of small, thin shapes (rows 3-14, widths 2-9 px) lying flat on the floor. It has no standing volume: no front face of 3+ rows, no front-edge line, no eave shadow, no ellipse and no roof or awning. The upper cluster (rows 3-6) is a small bone with a light highlight. The lower cluster (rows 8-13) is a few bone shafts with dark shading. Row 14 is a pale blue-grey strip. It reads as flat debris seen from above. For debris this is the expected form, so there is no bulky body that needs a top surface.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny grey-white bone scatter, smaller than one 16x16 tile, with only 8 distinct colours in total. It reads as a pale sprite of about 2-3 light tones on a dark background. It has no tinted outline, no grain, no per-bone shading and no clustered texture. The references (hedge, well, stall) carry 5-6 shading steps, material-toned outlines and dense texture dots. The tile-based measured facts are 0 because the piece is sub-tile, so I judged by eye. It is a sparse prop, but it is still thinner and flatter than the references and looks more like a sticker or icon than a shaded Beodeul prop. It does not pass at this scale next to the references.

surfaces.part: bottom strip of pale bluish bone/shard

answer.evidence: The drawing is a sparse scatter of small, flat pieces (rows 3-14) with gaps between them, such as a skull-like blob at rows 3-6 and elongated bones at rows 8-14. No piece has a front-edge line, eave shadow, ellipse or a vertical face of 3 or more rows. The pieces lie flat on the floor, as expected for debris, so no body has a top and a front face. This reads as a flat top-down layout with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny, sparse grey-white scatter of bones, about 8 distinct colours in total and smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile facts are 0 and I judged by eye. It reads as roughly 2-3 lightness steps (a light bone tone and a grey shadow) with no per-bone shading and no material-tone outline. It looks like a thin pale sticker next to the references, which carry 5-6 steps, tinted outlines and grain (hedge 9 tones per tile, stall 17, well 20). The sparseness alone would not fail it, but a careful artist would not accept it beside the references: it is flatter and thinner, with no texture, no cracks or ends on the bones, and no soil or ground shading to anchor it. Its outline is effectively absent, with the dark edge share at 0%, so it cannot count as a material-tone outline.
